purpose: One rule for choosing which encoding of a sample MS-DIAL analyses, with the cases both the Catalog and MS-DIAL Interactive must decide the same way. The Catalog applies it wherever a repository lists files; Interactive applies it after extraction, to files an archive held. Each case lists the paths of one unit and the role every path must end with.
rule: Files name the same sample when their basenames match with the container suffix removed; a per-sample archive (x.d.zip, x.mzML.gz) is read as the container it unpacks to, and a vendor folder listed through its members (x.raw/_FUNC001.DAT) as the folder.
Among files of one sample, a vendor container (.raw, .d, .wiff, .wiff2, .lcd, .qgd, .abf, .ibf, .cdf, .lrp) is analysed and every other encoding becomes raw_alternate.
With no vendor container, a converted container MS-DIAL reads (.mzML, .imzML) is analysed, and a format MS-DIAL cannot read becomes raw_alternate.
Two containers of equal preference are both left in place: no preference was stated between them, and none is invented.
A .wiff2 always wins over the .wiff of the same sample, decided by the analyst on 2026-09-21.

A format MS-DIAL cannot read (.mzXML, .mzData, .mgf, .ibd, .dat, .scan) is marked requires_conversion wherever it appears; only mzXML is marked for conversion to mzML (decided by the user on 2026-09-30).
Files inside a vendor folder are its members and never compete.

cases.name: packed vendor container beats packed mzML (MTBLS243)
two vendor containers: no preference is invented
mzXML alone is the input, marked for conversion to mzML
mzData alone is the input, with no conversion planned
